facts.text: Traction is the grip between a tire or track and the ground; on loose, wet or soft surfaces, reduced traction makes the ground rather than the brakes limit braking.
facts.quote: Traction is the grip between a tire or track and the ground, and on loose, wet or soft surfaces there is less of it, so braking is limited by the ground rather than by the brakes.

facts.text: On a slope, the booklet expresses the traction limit as a_traction = µ_min x g x cos θ - g x sin θ, where µ_min is the lowest friction expected and θ is the slope angle.
facts.quote: the traction limit as `a_traction = µ_min x g x cos θ - g x sin θ`, where µ_min is the lowest friction expected and θ the slope angle [Chapter 8].

facts.text: The booklet reports that tracks retain more shear force than tires in soft soil.
facts.quote: The booklet reports that tracks keep more shear force than tires in soft soil

facts.text: A 2023 soil model predicted forces well in sand, but its tuning parameters changed with slip angle; the reported testing used single-wheel rigs and sand, not full machines.
facts.quote: a 2023 soil model predicted forces well in sand but its tuning parameters changed with slip angle, and that all of this was tested on single-wheel rigs and sand, not full machines [Chapter 8].

facts.text: The booklet searched for but did not find a reliable table of friction values for wet dirt, gravel or mud adequate for setting braking thresholds.
facts.quote: Two things were searched for and not found: a reliable table of friction values for wet dirt, gravel or mud good enough to set braking thresholds

facts.text: The booklet searched for but did not find any published full-machine braking distance on wet clay or loose gravel.
facts.quote: and any published full-machine braking distance on wet clay or loose gravel [Chapter 8].

facts.text: Available braking must be treated as a distribution over machine, terrain and state and measured or estimated conservatively, rather than taken from a handbook coefficient.
facts.quote: Available braking has to be treated as a distribution over machine, terrain and state, measured or estimated conservatively, rather than read from a handbook coefficient [Chapter 8].

facts.text: The booklet recommends a low-speed surface matrix covering hard, loose and wet surfaces for each machine family, with detailed soil modeling only where simple envelopes fail to transfer.
facts.quote: The booklet recommends a low-speed surface matrix (hard, loose and wet) per machine family, with detailed soil modeling only where such simple envelopes fail to transfer [Chapter 8].
